summary: The Entry–Propagation–Recovery framework traces where conflicting memory first changes an agent action, how the effect propagates and whether recovery occurs. WebArena and the controlled MemTrapBench separate memory-consumption failures across these stages.

name: Tactile: Giving Computer-Using Agents Hands and Feet
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Tactile turns accessibility, OCR and visual evidence into explicit desktop targets with executable actions and verification cues. Its execution loop chooses semantic actions or coordinate fallbacks while retaining provenance for replay and diagnosis.

name: Falsifiable Commitment Planning for Self-Correcting Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces FCPAgent, which attaches confirming and falsifying evidence to each skill-grounded plan step. A plan–test–repair loop checks actions and observations, then localizes contradictions so execution, skills, or plans can be revised at the appropriate level.

name: How Benchmarks Mis-Score Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Audits failure-scored computer-use trajectories to distinguish agent errors from broken tasks and evaluator false negatives. It organizes reliability issues across task construction, trajectory evidence, scoring, and reporting, then derives corresponding evaluation design practices.

name: Why Are GUI Agents Correct but Late? Decode on the Decision-Time Critical Path, Tested with Pre-Compiled Policy Trees
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Adaptive Anticipatory Policy Trees, which precompute guarded actions and deadlines during idle periods so transient GUI events can be handled without new text generation. Paired experiments examine when this prepared execution helps and when reactive control remains preferable.

name: Rethinking Inference-Time Scaling in Local Computer-Use Agents: Failure Modes and Compute Tradeoffs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Examines inference-time scaling for local computer-use models by varying context, step budgets, decomposition, and parallel execution. OSWorld experiments track both task performance and changing failure modes, exposing cases where extra computation extends errors or adds coordination overhead.

name: "Allow" to Achieve, Over-Privileged Inadvertently: The Unintended Cost of Task-Completion-Driven Pop-up Decisions in Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: This permission-literacy study tests whether mobile GUI agents grant only task-necessary permissions. Controlled changes to task context and requester identity expose authorization biases and the trade-off between suppressing unnecessary and legitimate grants.

name: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Mobile Agent Evaluation
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: MobileJudgeBench compares completion judges against human labels on mobile-agent trajectories. It studies screenshot-sampling baselines, model-dependent error profiles and how judge quality relates to agent rankings and reinforcement-learning rewards.

name: SynWeaver: Website-Prior Task and Trajectory Co-Synthesis for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: SynWeaver explores a website to build a map of page states and executable interactions, then learns website priors for task proposals. Joint task/trajectory synthesis revises inconsistent pairs and verifies or repairs the resulting supervision.

name: ComponentBench: Diagnosing Component-Level Failures in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ComponentBench evaluates short interactions with canonical web UI components using verified tasks and matched human reference trajectories. Its diagnostic pipeline compares observation/action representations and analyzes structural difficulty, failure patterns and interaction efficiency.

name: Reflection with Action-Induced Visual Differences for Desktop GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Evidence-First Reflection, which separates extraction of action-induced screen changes from judgment of whether an operation achieved its objective. It filters visual differences into relevant evidence before a desktop agent’s reflector decides how execution should continue.

name: Are Android GUI Agents Robust Against Runtime Anomalies? AnTrap: Evaluating Agents in Dynamic Adversarial Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces AnTrap, which injects task-solvable runtime anomalies into Android GUI-agent trajectories using a layered failure taxonomy. It compares model robustness and adversarial reinforcement learning to distinguish recoverable interface traps from persistent contextual failures.

name: Learning Simple Test-Time Environments for LLM Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Test-Time Environment Decomposition, which uses trial interaction to break complex web observations into simpler modules. A label-free adaptation procedure learns from these sub-environments and studies whether their gains compose in full web tasks.

name: ElderBench: Benchmarking Autonomous Mobile Agents for Older Adults
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ElderBench evaluates mobile GUI agents on smartphone requests elicited from older adults, including indirect and underspecified language. Online and offline tests, instruction normalization and linguistic analyses examine how these request patterns contribute to failures.

name: AgentHijack: Visual Patch Attacks on Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AgentHijack evaluates whether visual patch effects propagate from screenshots through model outputs and action parsing into real environment changes. Its controlled web-page experiments distinguish intermediate attack signals from verified end-to-end consequences.

name: Learning from Reliable Negatives: Confidence-Anchored Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Confidence-Anchored Learning uses coordinate-token confidence to filter pseudo-supervision for GUI grounding. Its negative-only variant performs label-free test-time updates to reduce reliance on potentially incorrect positive examples.

name: EchoPath: Execution-Level Replayable Memory for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: EchoPath turns validated GUI trajectories into parameterized replay procedures with explicit runtime preconditions. Image-based target matching adjusts stored coordinates, while ambiguous steps fall back to bounded repair or fresh planning.

name: Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: EvoSkill-GUI revises reusable skill files from execution feedback through an executor–critic loop. It studies how training-free updates to localization, recovery and procedure information help subsequent mobile and desktop tasks.

name: ERPBench: A State-Grounded Evaluation Paradigm for Computer-Use Agents in Enterprise Software
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ERPBench evaluates screenshot-only agents in enterprise software using database values to check the business records produced by their actions. It pairs these state-based checks with a harness for human approval and analyzes cases where visible completion masks incorrect persisted data.

name: CAVEAT: Towards Robust Computer-Use Agents in Incentive-Misaligned Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CAVEAT, a controlled marketplace benchmark for testing whether delegated agents preserve user objectives when interfaces favor other outcomes. It diagnoses decision failures and studies harness interventions and targeted training to improve resistance to marketplace steering.

name: ScreenHaystack: Finding Blind Zones in GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Moves controlled target icons across high-resolution interfaces to diagnose spatial blind zones in grounding models and study targeted augmentation.

name: REBASE: Device-Cloud Experience Coherence for GUI Agents Across App Updates
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces REBASE, a device–cloud protocol for repairing cached GUI experience after app updates. It combines cloud replay, device-side step verification, and progressively richer failure reports to produce repairs tied to application versions.

name: GUITAR: Structured Failure Diagnosis of GUI Agents via State Transitions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces GUITAR, which groups visually different screens into functional states and analyzes agent failures over a state-transition graph. It uses the resulting bottlenecks to diagnose recurring mobile and web errors and evaluate targeted guidance.

name: Same Tasks, Different Apps: Why Mobile GUI Agents Fail to Generalize?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces AnyAppBench, a live Android benchmark that holds user goals fixed while changing the application used to achieve them. It combines category-controlled task pairs with failure annotations to distinguish task understanding from application-specific execution skill.

name: One Rollout Is All You Get: Fully Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Defines a test-time adaptation setting with one counted attempt per arriving GUI task and no ground-truth feedback. Its SOLO method filters or relabels completed episodes, then updates a small adapter from a short window of the agent’s own experience.

name: Before Acting, Change the State: Prospective State Intervention for Web Agents under Deceptive Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Veer, a runtime defense that changes task-relevant web state when an otherwise valid proposed action would produce an unauthorized consequence. It plans a prospective intervention and grounds and verifies its execution before the base agent continues.

name: WebPageBench: Event-Level Verification and Controlled UI-Variant Generation for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Verifies web tasks through typed interface events and generates controlled UI variations while preserving instructions and success conditions.

name: Constructing Challenging Browser-Use Tasks by Controlled Environment Interventions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: BreakingWeb pairs solvable browser tasks with controlled environment interventions that preserve the goal, target and backend success criterion. The paired evaluations isolate robustness failures, including agents declaring completion without the required state change.

name: Structured Interaction, Visual Localization, and Robust Execution for Complex Web Tasks: A Technical Report on the WebRetriever Challenge
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Describes a WebRetriever agent that combines semantic webpage operations with visual localization when structured representations are insufficient. Hierarchical context management and fault-aware execution support processing tasks across concurrent browsers.

name: PrecogUI: Proactive GUI Agents via Pre-cognitive Simulation and Experience Retrieval
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Presents PrecogUI, which retrieves prior anomaly and success patterns and predicts symbolic UI transitions before choosing actions. It also introduces InterfereBench, generated for evaluating long GUI workflows with disruptive events and recovery requirements.

name: Absorbed in Inertia: Activation Analysis for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies repetitive, unproductive actions in desktop agents through their internal activation states. It proposes Reset, Reroute, Restore, a context intervention that temporarily resets an agent’s trajectory and later restores it to help escape repeated ineffective behavior.

name: RealGUINoise: An Interactive Cross-Platform Benchmark for GUI Agent Robustness under Real-World Interface Noise
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Evaluates interactive GUI agents under varied realistic interface noise, comparing task completion, safety, and behavior with clean-environment runs.

name: Talk2Agent: Benchmarking Voice Interfaces for Text Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Talk2Agent, a benchmark of spoken instructions for computer-use tasks that measures whether voice interfaces preserve task-critical information. It pairs human speech with an execution-free intention-based metric and checks how that metric relates to downstream task completion.

name: Learning Reliable GUI Agents under Imperfect Priors
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Combines structured GUI exploration with training designed to tolerate imperfect retrieved experience. It builds state-transition graphs and synthetic task trajectories, then injects realistic forms of interface drift so agents learn when to rely on or reject prior guidance.

name: GUI-HARVEST: Self-Improving GUI Agents through Evidence-Driven Harness Evolution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Improves GUI-agent execution code by analyzing action effects and repeated-task failures, then validating bounded changes with frozen model weights.

name: WebFovea: When the Model Is Right but the Click Is Wrong -- Reliable Round Trips for Vision-Based Web Agents on Live Websites
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Describes WebFovea, a vision-based live-web agent whose execution loop checks action parsing, browser effects, feedback accuracy, and observation delivery. The report analyzes failures such as coordinate mismatches and silent control interactions and documents corresponding harness changes.

name: Decoupling What from Where: How Should a Small GUI Grounding Model Receive the Action Type?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Compares ways to condition a small GUI grounding model on action type under matched training conditions on Android in the Wild. The study traces apparent gains to a coordinate-serialization choice and reports limited evidence that the gains persist with predicted action types.

name: Can Agents Work for Everyone? Cross-User Reliability for Mobile GUI Agents in Personalized User Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces PAIR for controlled evaluation of mobile GUI agents across user-conditioned application states and RePAIR for training from cross-user subgoal outcomes. The study examines failures when personalized interfaces change which items an agent must identify.

name: When Charts Deceive Web Agents: A Paired Benchmark for Misleading Visualization-Grounded Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces MisVisAgentBench, a paired executable benchmark that changes chart evidence while holding web tasks fixed, to trace how misleading visualizations affect agent decisions and downstream actions.

name: ConClick: Element-Wise Contrastive Learning Improves GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Analyzes recurring distractor clicks in GUI grounding and introduces ConClick, a contrastive training method built from target–distractor pairs. Its ReClick inference procedure revisits candidate regions and compares competing predictions.

name: MHVF: Training-Free GUI Grounding via Verification-Guided Multi-Hypothesis Search
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces MHVF, a training-free grounding method that explores several candidate screen regions, verifies them in local views, and uses those checks to guide further search.

name: CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CLASHarness, generating verifiable computer-use tasks with conflicting agent reports, shared-state constraints, and coordination requirements to evaluate conflict detection and resolution.

name: How GUI Agents Fail: GraceBench for Execution Stability Diagnosis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced. Android platform tagging is additionally supported by the primary project documentation.
summary: Introduces GraceBench, using application transition graphs and recorded interaction evidence to diagnose deviations, loops, and recovery that final task-success scores can hide.
